Working notes — claims triage (CLM-7001–7010)

- Small paper claims with no inconsistencies (home power surge, health specialist consult) approved and settled. Paper filing alone is not a rejection reason.
- Large payout alone is not a rejection reason. Health claims rejected for large amount, paper channel, premiums being current, or pending verification were valid on appeal. Do not reject health claims on those grounds alone.
- Auto claims rejected for amount-to-damage mismatch or suspected inflation were valid on appeal. Treat mismatch as a cue for more evidence, not as sufficient rejection.
- Home online claims are high-risk. Approvals of online home burst-pipe/water-damage claims—large and small—were later found fraudulent. Require stronger independent verification before approving online home claims.
- “Photos pending” is ambiguous. It did not justify rejecting a health claim, but supported rejecting a home online large storm-damage claim later confirmed fraudulent. Use it with category/context, not alone.
- First claim on policy is not a reliable rejection reason: one approved and settled; one auto rejection was overturned.
- Administrative notes—docs scanned/attached, claimant reachable, call notes filed—do not establish legitimacy or fraud.
- Online approvals in this sample all later proved fraudulent. Before approving any online claim, seek corroboration beyond the portal filing.
- Paper small claims remain the safest approvals when details are consistent.
- Correct rejection so far: home online large storm damage with pending photos and confirmed fraud. Overturned rejections clustered around health large, auto large/mismatch, and proxies like channel/amount/first claim.

Guideline: decide on concrete evidence and category-specific red flags; avoid single-factor rejections.

Working notes — claims triage (CLM-7001–7020)

- Approve only on concrete evidence; avoid single-factor rejections. Channel, amount, first claim, premiums current, call notes/docs scanned/claimant reachable, and “photos pending” are neutral unless tied to category-specific fraud indicators.
- Online claims are high-risk, including health. No online approval in this sample has proven valid; one health online small with pending photos was approved then found fraudulent. Require strong independent corroboration before approving any online claim.
- Online home rejections are often valid when fraud is confirmed, but not automatic. A large online home power-surge first claim rejected on those factors alone was overturned. Reject online home only with concrete/category red flags, not amount/first claim/channel alone.
- Phone/paper home break-in claims have settled valid across small/large, first claim, premiums-current, and photos-pending notes. Treat as lower risk when details are consistent.
- Health phone large approved and settled. Online health remains risky; pending photos did not make approval safe.
- Paper small consistent claims remain safe approvals.
- First claim and premiums-current are not rejection reasons.
- Administrative notes are not proof of legitimacy or fraud.
- Confirmed fraudulent rejections: online home small power surge, small storm, small break-in; earlier online home large storm.
- Overturned/bad outcomes: online home large power surge first claim rejection overturned; health online small photos pending approved then fraudulent.

Guideline: decide on concrete evidence and category-specific red flags.

Working notes — claims triage (CLM-7001–7030)

- Decide on concrete, category-specific evidence. Channel, amount, first claim, premiums-current, photos pending, notes/docs scanned, claimant reachable are neutral unless tied to fraud indicators.
- First claim, premiums-current, and administrative notes never justify rejection.
- Online health: high risk. Reject unless strong independent corroboration. Confirmed fraudulent: small with docs scanned; small with claimant reachable; earlier small photos pending approved then fraudulent.
- Online home: high risk. Reject only with concrete/category red flags. Confirmed fraud: small power surge, small storm, small break-in; large storm. Do not reject large power-surge first claim on those factors alone (overturned).
- Online auto: do not reject solely on online/amount. Large sideswipe and small sideswipe rejected without corroboration were overturned on appeal as valid. Need concrete red flags or strong corroboration before rejecting.
- Phone/paper home break-in: lower risk when details consistent. Approved/settled: paper small first claim; phone large. Phone home power surge small photos pending approved.
- Phone health: lower risk when consistent. Approved/settled: small first claim; small dental photos pending.
- Paper small consistent claims remain safe approvals.
- Auto caution: paper large rear-end with no noted auto red flags was approved then found fraudulent. Absence of noted auto indicators is not proof; require corroboration for large auto.
- Guideline: approve on concrete evidence; reject on concrete/category-specific red flags, not channel/amount alone.

Working notes — claims triage (CLM-7001–7040)

- Use concrete, category-specific evidence. Channel, amount, first claim, premiums-current, photos pending, notes/docs scanned, claimant reachable are neutral alone.
- Never reject solely on first claim, premiums-current, administrative notes, or amount.
- Auto: large auto requires corroboration/concrete red flags. Large paper auto with only docs scanned/no red flags: reject; confirmed fraud. Small paper auto sideswipe with reachable claimant approved/settled. Online auto: do not reject solely on online/amount; prior large/small sideswipe rejections were overturned as valid.
- Health: large paper health claims are high risk. Reachable, premiums-current, photos pending, first claim, referral, docs scanned do not make them safe: several were approved then found fraudulent. Require strong corroboration or concrete red flags; consider rejection. Phone health lower risk when consistent (approved: small first claim; small dental photos pending). Online health: small online/docs scanned rejection was overturned valid, but confirmed fraud exists for small online health; do not auto-reject on online/docs alone—need red flags/strong corroboration.
- Home: phone/paper small power surge with no red flags settled. Paper home large burst pipe with reachable claimant was approved then fraudulent: large home needs corroboration. Phone/paper home break-in lower risk when details consistent.
- Paper small consistent claims remain safe approvals, e.g., small auto.
- Guideline: approve on concrete evidence; reject on concrete/category-specific red flags, not channel/amount alone.

Working notes — claims triage (CLM-7001–7050)

- Use concrete, category-specific evidence. Reject on concrete/category red flags, not channel/amount alone. Neutral alone: channel, amount, first claim, premiums-current, photos pending, notes/docs scanned, claimant reachable, call notes, referral.
- Auto: Large auto requires corroboration/red flags. Large paper auto with only docs scanned/no red flags: reject; confirmed fraud. Small paper auto sideswipe with reachable claimant: approve/settled. Online auto: do not reject on online/amount alone; prior rejections overturned. Large phone auto with reachable only: reject overturned valid—need red flags.
- Health: Large paper health is high risk. Reachable, premiums-current, photos pending, first claim, referral, call notes, docs scanned do not make it safe. Reject large paper health often correct; confirmed fraud (CLM-7042, 7050). Large online/phone health: do not reject on amount/channel/reachable/referral/no corroboration alone; rejections overturned valid (7041, 7049). Small paper health can be fraudulent even with docs scanned/no red flags (7043); approve cautiously only with corroboration. Small online health with photos pending can settle (7048). Phone health lower risk when consistent.
- Home: Small paper/phone home with consistent details/first claim: approve/settled (7046). Large home (paper/phone) with only photos pending/reachable: reject overturned valid—need concrete corroboration/red flags. Large paper burst pipe approved then fraudulent; large home remains high risk.
- Paper small auto/home consistent remain safe; do not generalize to health.

Working notes — claims triage (CLM-7001–7060)

General: Use concrete category-specific evidence. Reject on red flags, not channel/amount alone. Neutral: channel, amount, first claim, premiums-current, reachable, referral, call notes, docs scanned, photos pending. Small paper auto/home consistent remain safe; do not generalize to health.

Auto:
- Small paper/phone: approve if consistent/reachable/first claim (7052, 7060).
- Large paper: reject if only docs scanned/no red flags; confirmed fraud.
- Online large: do not reject on online/amount/first claim alone; prior rejections overturned (7054). Need concrete inconsistency.
- Large phone: high risk. Rejections with only reachable overturned—need red flags; but approval on first claim/no red flags can be fraudulent (7058). Require corroboration.

Health:
- Large paper: high risk; reject often correct even with call notes/reachable/premiums-current/docs (7042,7050,7055). Confirmed fraud.
- Small paper: can be fraudulent even with premiums-current/docs/no red flags (7043,7051); approve only with concrete corroboration.
- Large online/phone: do not reject on amount/channel/reachable/referral/no corroboration alone (7041,7049); phone can settle if consistent (7056). Phone lower risk than paper.

Home:
- Small paper/phone consistent/first claim: approve/settled (7046).
- Large home: high risk; need concrete category-specific support. Rejections on routine evidence—call notes, photos, reachable, first claim—often overturned valid (7053,7059). Large online can approve/settle if routine and no red flags (7057). Large paper burst pipe approved then fraudulent—remain cautious.
